previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of orthotopic liver transplant, chronic kidney disease, gastrostomy dependence, and chronic lower extremity edema, was admitted for worsening left leg swelling and erythema following a blister rupture, concerning for cellulitis. He was initially treated with IV vancomycin and evaluated for deep vein thrombosis, which was ruled out by Doppler ultrasound. The patient showed clinical improvement, with reduced edema and erythema, and was transitioned to oral cephalexin and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim for a ten-day course. Wound care was optimized, and he was advised to hold topical clobetasol during antibiotic treatment. His kidney function remained stable, and he was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans and instructions for leg elevation and future use of compression therapy.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of large intestine

Brief Hospital Course:
Summary
___ with history of alcoholic cirrhosis s/p liver transplant 
(___) on MMF and prednisone presented with nausea, vomiting, 
and diarrhea. He was found to have ___ on CKD from combination 
hypovolemia and acute urinary retention. 

Acute issues
# Urinary retention and ___
Urinary catheter was placed, and patient received IVF repletion. 
Renal function returned to baseline by HD #2. Patient underwent 
a void trial on HD#3 and passed without difficulty. 

# Nausea and vomiting
Infectious workup, including norovirus, did not identify any 
obvious cause of patient's symptoms. TF were held for 5 days, 
but patients symptoms did not worsen or improve. Patient was 
planned to have a flexible sigmoidoscopy for further evaluation 
of his symptoms, but patient refused the procedure. However, he 
was able to consistently tolerate oral feedings with minimal 
symptoms and so was discharged home.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr ___,

You were admitted to ___ because you were having nausea, 
vomiting, and diarrhea. You also had some retention of urine and 
had worsening of your kidney function. For your kidney injury 
and urinary retention, we placed a urinary catheter. We gave you 
intravenous fluids and your kidney function improved to normal. 
We performed a series of tests which did not identify a serious 
underlying cause for your symptoms. However, with treatment and 
time, your symptoms improved and your were able to tolerate oral 
feeds. We would have like to perform a procedure called a 
flexible sigmoidoscopy to look for sources of your diarrhea, but 
you refused this procedure. You will be discharged home with 
follow-up appointments in clinic. 

Please take all medications as prescribed and keep all scheduled 
appointments. Should you develop a recurrence of the same 
symptoms that originally brought you to the hospital, experience 
any of the warning signs listed below, or experience any other 
symptoms that concern you, please seek medical attention. 

It was a pleasure taking care of you!
Your ___ Care Team
